selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the passage invite the reader to understand by thinking about a short comparison?
questions.answer: It invites the reader to understand the purpose of the world, why human beings were created, and the mystery of the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: In the comparison, what kind of person is introduced first?
questions.answer: A king with great wealth, knowledge, skills, and learning.

questions.question: What kinds of treasures did the king have?
questions.answer: He had many valuable treasures, including precious stones and other hidden wonderful riches.

questions.question: Besides wealth, what other strengths did the king have?
questions.answer: He had masterful skills in unusual arts, wide knowledge of amazing sciences, and deep learning.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a person who has beauty and perfection naturally want?
questions.answer: Such a person wants to see those qualities and also show them.

questions.question: What did the king want to establish in order to make his qualities known?
questions.answer: He wanted to set up an exhibition with displays.

questions.question: What four things did the king want people to notice through that exhibition?
questions.answer: He wanted them to see the greatness of his rule, his shining wealth, the wonders of his art, and the marvels of his knowledge.

questions.question: The passage says the king wanted to view his own beauty and perfection in two ways. What is the first way?
questions.answer: He wanted to behold them himself with his own aware and understanding sight.

questions.question: What is the second way the king wanted to view his beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: He wanted to see them through how others looked at them.

questions.question: What does this comparison suggest about why the king arranged the exhibition?
questions.answer: It suggests that the exhibition was made to reveal what he possessed and to let both he and others witness his excellence.

questions.question: What Qur’anic verses are placed at the beginning of the passage about?
questions.answer: They point to signs in creation such as the sun, moon, day, night, sky, earth, and the human self.

questions.question: After these verses, what does the speaker ask the reader to do?
questions.answer: The reader is asked to reflect on a brief comparison along with the speaker’s own self.

questions.question: Why is the king in the comparison described as having both visible and hidden treasures?
questions.answer: This shows that his riches were not limited to what people could easily see and that he possessed deeper wonders too.

questions.question: What do the king’s many arts and sciences tell us about him?
questions.answer: They show that he was highly capable, knowledgeable, and full of excellence.

questions.question: What desire moved the king to open a public display?
questions.answer: He wanted his beauty and perfection to become known and seen.

questions.question: Was the exhibition only for the people’s benefit, or did it also serve the king in some way? Explain.
questions.answer: It served both, because people would see his greatness, and he would also behold his qualities in two ways.

questions.question: What is one way the king wanted to witness his own excellence directly?
questions.answer: He wanted to see it himself with his own discerning sight.

questions.question: What is one way the king wanted to witness his own excellence indirectly?
questions.answer: He wanted to look at it as reflected in the awareness and view of others.

questions.question: What main idea ties the whole passage together?
questions.answer: A being with great beauty and perfection wants those qualities to be manifested and observed.

questions.question: In this passage, is the king presented as lacking greatness or as already possessing it? How do you know?
questions.answer: He is presented as already possessing it, because the passage lists his treasures, skills, knowledge, and learning before describing the exhibition.

questions.question: What three big topics does the passage say can be understood a little through the comparison?
questions.answer: The world’s purpose, the creation of human beings, and the mystery of the prayers.

questions.question: Who says this comparison is considered together with his own nafs?
questions.answer: The speaker says it is considered together with his own self.

questions.question: What does the king’s ownership of priceless jewels suggest about his condition?
questions.answer: It suggests he was extremely wealthy and possessed rare riches.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention hidden treasures as well as open ones?
questions.answer: To show that the king had deeper stores of wonder beyond what appeared on the surface.

title: 11 Word Introduction to the Parable and the Sultan's Purpose
